newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa wage talks still deadlocked.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa wage talks still deadlocked.

text.p: The latest round of wage talks between German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG and its 50,000 workers is still deadlocked, one of the main unions involved in the talks said on Thursday.

"The employer had already demanded a pay freeze ahead of the negotiations, and further talks are becoming exceptionally difficult as a result," Manfred Maertzke, chief negotiator for the OeTV transport and public sector union, said.

OetV said it was asking for a 2.3 percent pay increase and was seeking agreement with Lufthansa, which has signalled its aim to make cost cuts in the face of growing competition, on job protection guarantees.
White collar union DAG, which is holding parallel talks with the airline, is seeking a four percent pay increase.
A Lufthansa executive said earlier on Thursday that the airline had lost 250,000 clients and 50 million marks in sales to discount offers from rival airlines in the first half.
